name: Can you live in the house during a gut renovation?

mainEntity.name: Is it realistic to stay in a home while a full gut renovation is happening in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Is it realistic to stay in a home while a full gut renovation is happening in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in the house depends on how much of the home is being rebuilt and which systems will be offline. If the renovation includes kitchen and bathroom demolition, electrical or plumbing shutdowns, or major structural work, daily life becomes very difficult. Dust, noise, water interruptions, and construction crews moving through the property can also make the home unsafe or unlivable. In luxury renovations, homeowners often choose to relocate temporarily to protect health, reduce stress, and keep the schedule moving. If you plan to stay, the builder should define safe zones, active work hours, utility continuity, and whether temporary fixtures or partitions are possible. In many true gut renovations, the best practical decision is to move out until the rough construction phase is finished.
acceptedAnswer.description: Living in a home during a gut renovation is usually difficult and sometimes unsafe because the work can shut off utilities, create dust, block kitchens and bathrooms, and leave open walls or floors. Some homeowners stay only during limited phases, but many move out until major construction is complete.
